question.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=-2\pm 5\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-7.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 1∓\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
